proposals.before: The emperor agreed and appointed Xiangru commandant of palace attendants, giving him the credenza and dispatching him as chief envoy.
proposals.after: The emperor agreed and appointed Xiangru commandant of palace attendants, giving him the credentials and dispatching him as chief envoy.
proposals.reason: 建節 means bearing imperial credentials/insignia (節); “credenza” is an unrelated furniture sense and invents the wrong word.

proposals.before: If your words were true, Shu would never have adopted Han costume nor Ba Han manners—and I would still shrink from such talk.
proposals.after: If your words were true, Shu would never have adopted Han costume nor would Ba have changed its manners—and I would still shrink from such talk.
proposals.reason: 巴不化俗 means Ba would not have transformed its customs; “Ba Han manners” fuses Ba with Han and drops the verb.

proposals.before: now you would yoke them to the tribes of the west. Popular strength is spent; we doubt the task can ever be completed. That would be the envoys' legacy as well, and we tremble for your advisors.
proposals.after: now you would yoke them to the tribes of the west. Popular strength is spent; we doubt the task can ever be completed. This too would be the envoys' fault, and we privately worry for those at your side.
proposals.reason: 使者…累 means the envoys' burden/fault; “legacy” is the wrong sense of 累.

proposals.before: In cover Zhou leaped fish, fell grain vessel, rested them with burning.
proposals.after: For Zhou, a fish leaped and grain fell into the vessel; they were honored by burning them as offerings.
proposals.reason: 蓋 is an explanatory particle (“for/indeed”), not “in cover”; the gloss is unintelligible and misreads the Zhou omen.

proposals.before: The house of Zhou received its sign when fish leaped into the king's boat and grain filled the vessel—then offered them up with fire.
proposals.after: The house of Zhou received its sign when a white fish leaped into King Wu's boat, and he offered it to Heaven in a burnt sacrifice.
proposals.reason: The omen is a white fish leaping into King Wu's boat; the source says nothing about grain, and the fish alone is offered in sacrifice.

decisions.after: The emperor agreed and appointed Xiangru General of the Household, sending him as an envoy bearing imperial credentials.
decisions.reason: 建節往使 means Xiangru went as an envoy bearing imperial credentials; “credenza” is an unrelated furniture word, and the source does not make him a chief envoy.

decisions.after: If what you say were true, it would mean that Shu had never changed its dress and Ba had never reformed its customs. Even I cannot bear to hear such an argument.
decisions.reason: 巴不化俗 means Ba would not have transformed its customs; “Ba Han manners” wrongly fuses Ba with Han and drops the verb 化.

decisions.after: now you would link them with the tribes of the west. The people's strength is exhausted, and we fear the work cannot be completed. This would also become a liability for you as envoy, and we privately fear for you.
decisions.reason: 使者 is the single envoy being addressed, Sima Xiangru; 累 is a burden or liability, not a legacy, and 左右 is a respectful circumlocution for the addressee here.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 此亦使者之累也，竊為左右患之

decisions.after: For Zhou, a fish leaped into the boat, and it was marked as auspicious with a burnt offering.
decisions.reason: 蓋 is the particle “for/indeed,” and 躍魚隕杭 is the Zhou omen of a fish leaping into the boat (杭=舟), then honored with 燎; the original is nonsense, but the proposal wrongly invents “grain” falling into a vessel.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 蓋周躍魚隕杭，休之以燎

decisions.reason: The parallel accounts and Yan Shigu's note identify a white fish leaping into King Wu's boat and being offered to Heaven; the source contains no grain or second offering.

sourceWitness.citation: Hanshu 67, Yan Shigu note at s0207
sourceWitness.excerpt: 蓋周躍魚隕杭，休之以燎
